argument_markdown:
## 1. A finite-etale elliptic cover of M_{0,4}

Put B=P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, identified with M_{0,4}. Let Cbar be the smooth projective curve with function field C(x,y), y^3=x(x-1), and let C be obtained from Cbar by deleting the points above 0, 1, and infinity. The degree-three map g:Cbar→P^1 induced by x is totally ramified exactly above 0, 1, and infinity: the valuations of x(x-1) there are 1, 1, and -2, none divisible by 3. Riemann-Hurwitz gives

2g(Cbar)-2=3(-2)+3(3-1)=0,

so Cbar has genus one. After deleting the three ramification points, g:C→B is finite etale of degree three.

For the smooth affine curve C, compact-support localization for C⊂Cbar gives

Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C;Q)=H^1(Cbar;Q),

which has nonzero types (1,0) and (0,1), while H_c^2(C;Q)=Q(-1), of type (1,1).

## 2. A non-Tate degree-16 corner over M_{0,18}

Rigidifying the first three markings to 0, 1, and infinity identifies

M_{0,18}={(z_1,...,z_15) in B^15 : z_i≠z_j for i≠j}.

Define

Mtilde=C^15 ×_{B^15} M_{0,18}.

It is a nonempty irreducible finite-etale cover of M_{0,18}. Its complement Y=C^15 minus Mtilde is the union of the inverse images of the pairwise diagonals z_i=z_j, hence dim Y≤14.

Compact-support Kunneth gives a direct summand

Q(-1) tensor (Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C;Q))^{tensor 14}

inside Gr^W_16 H_c^16(C^15;Q): choose H_c^2(C) from one factor and H_c^1(C) from the other fourteen. Choosing the (1,0) part in each of those fourteen factors gives a nonzero Hodge component of type

(1,1)+14(1,0)=(15,1).

Let alpha denote a nonzero class in this component. For any separated complex variety T of dimension at most 14, F^15 H_c^k(T;C)=0: this follows from a smooth hyperresolution and the compact-support logarithmic de Rham complex, whose forms have degree at most dim T. Therefore F^15H_c^16(Y;C)=0.

Localization contains

H_c^16(Mtilde;Q)→H_c^16(C^15;Q)→H_c^16(Y;Q).

Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for both filtrations. The image of alpha in H_c^16(Y) must be zero because it would have type (15,1), while F^15H_c^16(Y)=0. Exactness and strictness therefore yield a nonzero type-(15,1) class

alphatilde in Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Mtilde;Q).

Thus this degree-16 corner is already non-Tate.

## 3. Transport to a balanced tetragonal atlas component

By ATT-0112/CLM-0112-2, CLM-0112-4, and CLM-0112-7, Hbar^bal is smooth of pure dimension 15, and its non-simply-branched locus has dimension at most 14. Hence its simply-branched open is nonempty.

Consider the Hurwitz space Hord^sb of connected simply-branched degree-four genus-six covers with their eighteen branch points ordered, modulo PGL_2 on the target. The classical Hurwitz local-deformation theorem makes the branch map

b:Hord^sb→M_{0,18}

etale. It is finite: over an ordered branch configuration, a connected cover is specified by a transitive tuple of eighteen transpositions in S_4 with product one, modulo simultaneous conjugacy, and only finitely many such tuples exist; analytic continuation of these tuples gives a finite covering. Moreover, a transitive group generated by transpositions is S_4, whose centralizer in S_4 is trivial, so these covers have no target-preserving automorphisms and Hord^sb is a scheme.

Choose a connected component X of Hord^sb whose balanced open Xbal is nonempty; such a component exists by the preceding nonemptiness. Base-change along Mtilde→M_{0,18}, and choose a connected component Xtilde of X×_{M_{0,18}}Mtilde meeting the balanced locus. Then

f:Xtilde→Mtilde

is connected finite etale of some positive degree d. Since Mtilde is irreducible and Xtilde is connected and normal, Xtilde is irreducible. Finite-etale pullback and trace on compactly supported cohomology satisfy

Tr_f composed with f^*=d times identity.

Consequently f^*(alphatilde) is nonzero and has type (15,1) in Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Xtilde;Q).

Let V=Xtilde∩Xbal. It is a nonempty open in the irreducible smooth 15-fold Xtilde, hence connected, and its complement T has dimension at most 14. Applying localization once more,

H_c^16(V;Q)→H_c^16(Xtilde;Q)→H_c^16(T;Q),

and using F^15H_c^16(T;C)=0, shows that f^*(alphatilde) lifts to a nonzero type-(15,1) class in

Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;Q).

The morphism V→Hbar^bal is etale. Adjoining V to any separated finite-type etale atlas of Hbar^bal gives another such atlas, with V as a connected component. Thus V is an allowed scheme-atlas component in precisely the scope used by FND-0167.

## 4. Contradiction to the exact theorem

A direct sum of Q(-8) is pure of type (8,8), so it has no Hodge component of type (15,1). We have proved

Gr^{15,1} Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;C)≠0.

Therefore Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;Q) is not a direct sum of Q(-8). This is exactly the j=8 case of the constant-coefficient hypothesis (H-S) that the exact theorem expressly includes among the required balanced-base and universal-curve corners under FND-0165 and FND-0167.

A theorem containing a universally asserted conjunct is disproved by one allowed atlas component on which that conjunct fails. Hence the exact C66-TATE-SUPPORT theorem is false as stated. This argument neither uses nor asserts FND-0164's prohibited transfer to constructible coefficients: every cohomology group used has constant Q-coefficients, and the only functorial operations are compact-support Kunneth, open-closed localization, and finite-etale pullback/trace. Nothing is asserted about the global kernel K, a map from Z to M_{6,6}, Gysin, support exhaustion, or RED-0001.

claims.statement: The normalization of y^3=x(x-1) is a genus-one curve, and deleting the points over 0, 1, and infinity gives a connected finite-etale degree-three cover C→M_{0,4} with Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C)=H^1(Cbar) non-Tate.

For Mtilde=C^15×_{(M_{0,4})^15}M_{0,18}, Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Mtilde;Q) has a nonzero Hodge component of type (15,1), obtained from Q(-1) tensor H^1(Cbar)^{tensor 14}; it survives removal of the inverse images of the diagonals because their dimension is at most 14.

Finite-etale pullback and trace transport the nonzero type-(15,1) class to a connected simply-branched tetragonal Hurwitz chart, and compact-support localization transports it further to its nonempty balanced open V.
The balanced open V is a connected component of an allowed separated finite-type etale scheme atlas of Hbar^bal, and Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;Q) is not a direct sum of Q(-8).
Because the exact theorem explicitly includes the (H-S) degree-16 constant-coefficient corner for every allowed atlas component, CLM-0118-4 is a counterexample and disproves the exact theorem.

novelty_claims: An explicit finite-etale atlas refinement, built from the elliptic Kummer cover y^3=x(x-1) of M_{0,4}, carries a nonzero type-(15,1) class in Gr^W_16 H_c^16 and disproves the universally included (H-S) degree-16 corner.

proof_dependencies.note: Dual-confirmed geometric dependency. CLM-0112-2 and CLM-0112-7 supply smoothness and pure dimensions 18 and 15 for the balanced fixed-target and quotient stacks; CLM-0112-4 supplies the codimension-one bound for the non-simply-branched locus.
Compact-support localization and strictness at the weight-equals-degree corner; the proof independently applies the same constant-coefficient localization argument.
Identifies (H-S) for j=8 as the assertion that Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;Q) is a sum of Q(-8), one of the constant-coefficient corners expressly included in the exact theorem.

summary: The exact theorem is false as written. Its explicitly included (H-S) degree-16 assertion fails after a legitimate finite-etale refinement of the simply-branched balanced atlas. A cyclic degree-three elliptic cover C→M_{0,4} produces a finite-etale cover of M_{0,18} whose degree-16 compactly supported cohomology contains Hodge type (15,1). This class survives removal of the pairwise diagonals, finite-etale pullback to a simply-branched Hurwitz chart, and restriction to the balanced open. The resulting connected atlas component V therefore has nonzero H^{15,1} in Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;Q), so that corner is not a sum of Q(-8). Since the exact theorem expressly includes all constant-coefficient corners required by FND-0167, this supplies a complete counterexample to the stated theorem.

theorem_scope.counterexample_base: a connected component V of a separated finite-type etale scheme atlas of Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2]
excluded: the global kernel K in H^16(Mbar_{6,6})
any embedding, Gysin map, image, or support-exhaustion statement in M_{6,6}
theorem_scope.failed_conjunct: the included constant-coefficient corner (H-S) for j=8: Gr^W_16 H_c^16(V;Q) must be a direct sum of Q(-8)

theorem_statement: Over C with Q-coefficients, on the balanced Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure model Z=Ord(U) of a (CE)+(N)+(BAL) genus-six degree-four family on a reduced locally Noetherian scheme atlas of the balanced tetragonal stack as in the dual-confirmed ATT-0112, prove that the exact target graded piece of the H_alpha-object of Z is Tate of type Q(8) in Borel-Moore degree 16 (equivalently Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q) is a direct sum of Q(-8)). This includes the simply-branched and complementary non-simply-branched loci, every S_6-isotypic component, and the constant-coefficient corners of the balanced base and universal curve needed under FND-0165 and FND-0167. Do not identify this with the global kernel K=ker(H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q)->H^{16}(D;Q)) (FND-0168). Do not construct a closed embedding, Gysin map, image, or support-exhaustion statement in M_{6,6}. This lemma does not resolve the campaign Hodge/Tate group RED-0001.
